sections.name: Abisko-Abiskojaure

difficulty.label: Easy walking; low technical difficulty
difficulty.source: Naturkartan describes the path as broad/easy with some boardwalk; STF does not provide a formal grade.

notes: Official section direction is Abisko to Abiskojaure.
This section overlaps Kungsleden and Nordkalottleden.
The whole stage lies in Abisko National Park.
At Abiskojaure, the hut area is reached by leaving the Kungsleden through-route and crossing Kamajakka by suspension bridge; later section joins may need to avoid duplicating this hut access spur.

start.label: Kungsledsportalen / Kungsleden trailhead, Abisko
caveats: This is the route/trailhead coordinate, not the STF building coordinate.
About 93 m from OSM trailhead node 289461132 and about 186 m from the OSM STF Abisko Turiststation point.
STF Abiskojaure page says the Kungsleden trail toward Abiskojaure starts about 300 m from the bus stop, railway station and car park.

end.label: Abiskojaure hut area / Kungsleden section end
caveats: Naturkartan says hikers leave Kungsleden and cross Kamajakka by suspension bridge to reach the Abiskojaure cabins.
End coordinate is about 7 m from the OSM route end and about 32 m from the OSM Abiskojaure hut point.

sourceSummary.classification: planning-grade

caveats: STF says 15 km and 4-6 hours; Naturkartan says 14.0 km and 4-5 hours; AllTrails and OSM-derived sources are around 14-15 km. Use STF's 15 km / 4-6 h for official section display, and record 14.0 km Naturkartan linework distance as geometry metadata.
Official descriptions present Abiskojaure hut/cabin as the stage end, while Naturkartan notes hikers leave Kungsleden and cross Kamajakka by suspension bridge to reach the cabins.
Sources spell the mid-stage designated campsite as Nissonjohka, Nissunjohka, Nissunjakka/Nissunjåkka, and Nissonjåhka.

One AllTrails review from 2025-08-06 reported a bridge closure making the trail impassable without rerouting, but official sources checked on 2026-04-29 did not show a standing section closure and the bridge was not identified.
Naturkartan page linework is available in the web map/API evidence, but the public .gpx URL returned HTTP 500 on 2026-04-29 and the geometry agent found publish_gpx=false.

sections.name: Abiskojaure-Alesjaure

difficulty.label: Moderate mountain stage; no formal official grade found
difficulty.source: STF and Naturkartan describe a long 21 km stage with a 300 m climb at Kieronbacken, stony/wet stretches, open alpine terrain and possible water scarcity after Siellajohka, but do not publish a formal difficulty grade.

notes: Official section direction is Abiskojaure to Alesjaure.
This section overlaps Kungsleden and Nordkalottleden/Arctic Trail context in official and OSM sources.

The stage starts at the Abiskojaure hut area inside Abisko National Park, crosses Kamajakka back to the through-route, leaves the national park after a few kilometres, and ends at the Alesjaure hut area.
The Alesjaure boat across Alisjavri is an optional shortcut of about 6 km and should be modelled as access/shortcut metadata, not as mandatory hiking geometry.

start.label: Abiskojaure hut area / Kungsleden section start
caveats: Naturkartan/GPX geometry is stored Alesjaure-to-Abiskojaure and must be reversed for official section order.
The start is the hut-area/route endpoint. Hikers cross Kamajakka back to the through-route after leaving the hut area, so section-join import must avoid duplicating the Abiskojaure hut spur.

end.label: Alesjaure hut area / Kungsleden section end
caveats: Endpoint is near the Alesjaure hut area, not necessarily the cabin building centroid.
Optional boat terminal and hut subfacility coordinates should remain access/facility metadata until verified from official/operator sources.

sourceSummary.classification: planning-grade

caveats: Official section order and route title are Abiskojaure to Alesjaure, while Naturkartan GPX/API linework is stored Alesjaure to Abiskojaure.
Naturkartan API reports publish_gpx=false for site 14092, but the public GPX URL returned HTTP 200 application/gpx+xml on 2026-04-29.
Official sources display 21 km. Naturkartan computed GPX/API line is about 20.66 km, while Waymarked/OSM assembles about 20.36 km.

Official STF boat page updated 2025-07-05 lists Alesjaure shuttle schedule and payment context until further notice, but field report claims a 2025 shutdown and STF page has a general cash note versus Alesjaure-specific card/currency note.
OSM ferry way evidence includes useful operator/terminal hints, but the line geometry is duplicated/malformed with a clearly wrong full length.
Official sources provide terrain notes but no formal difficulty grade.
The route clearly starts in Abisko National Park and leaves it after a few kilometres, but no separate protected-area rule set was confirmed for the post-park segment in this batch.
Several child amenities at Alesjaure and exact Siellajohka/Radunjarga subfacility points rely on OSM support while official pages confirm the facility type but not exact coordinates.

sections.name: Alesjaure-Tjaktja

difficulty.label: Moderate mountain stage; no formal official grade found
difficulty.source: STF describes mostly easy walking at first, then steeper and rockier final kilometres. Naturkartan describes open moor, increasing stone/barrenness, Sielmmanjira ford and the climb toward Tjaktja.

notes: Official STF section direction is Alesjaure to Tjaktja.
This section overlaps Kungsleden and Nordkalottleden/Arctic Trail context.
STF publishes Alesjaure-Tjaktja as a 13 km day stage, while Naturkartan publishes the official county linework as a combined 25 km Alesjaure-Salka route with Tjaktja as an intermediate hut.
No ferry or boat belongs to this section; the Alesjaure boat is a section-2 shortcut/access record.

start.label: STF Alesjaure Mountain Cabin / Alesjaure section start
caveats: Naturkartan combined Alesjaure-Salka GPX appears to start on the main trail/bridge-side line, not exactly at the STF hut coordinate.
Section 2 and section 3 both use Alesjaure hut-area endpoints; import should avoid duplicating local hut/bridge spurs.

end.label: STF Tjaktja Mountain Cabin / Tjaktja section end
caveats: Decide whether section import should end at the STF hut GPS or at the Kungsleden mainline point near the hut.
Verify side-spur/access geometry to the hut before treating route geometry as navigation-grade.

sourceSummary.classification: planning-grade

caveats: STF lists Alesjaure-Tjaktja as section 3, 13 km, while Naturkartan publishes Alesjaure-Salka as one 25 km route with Tjaktja as an intermediate cabin.
STF hut coordinates are official facility endpoints, but both Naturkartan cut line and OSM/Waymarked section line are about 216-220 m from the STF Tjaktja hut coordinate.

No named land reserve or national park was confirmed for this section, but possible Natura 2000 water-system relevance was noted and exact overlap was not verified.
Alesjaure/Tjaktja child amenities, wild tent areas, Meditationsplats and Tjaktja waterfall rely on OSM or field evidence rather than official object coordinates.

sections.name: Tjaktja-Salka

difficulty.label: Moderate mountain pass stage; no formal official grade found
difficulty.source: STF gives no formal difficulty grade. Official and field sources describe a short but exposed stage over Tjaktjapasset, Kungsleden's highest point, with stony terrain, snow that can linger into July, scarce water near the pass and a steep/stony descent toward Salka.

notes: Official STF section direction is Tjaktja to Salka.
This is STF Abisko-Nikkaluokta stage 4 and the southern half of Naturkartan/Lansstyrelsen route BD31 Alesjaure-Salka.
The stage crosses Tjaktjapasset about 4 km south of Tjaktja. STF and Naturkartan describe this as Kungsleden's highest point at about 1150 m.
No ferry or boat belongs directly to this section. Boat services relevant to Alesjaure or Laddjujavri are adjacent access/stage-chain metadata, not section-4 route geometry.
Salka is a junction for the main Kungsleden south toward Singi and side routes toward Nallo and Hukejaure.

start.label: STF Tjaktja Mountain Cabin / Tjaktja section start
caveats: The mapped trail-stage boundary does not coincide exactly with the STF hut coordinate.
OSM relation 10861494 starts about 328 m from the STF Tjaktja hut, at the same point where OSM relation 10861495 Alesjaure-Tjaktja ends.
Naturkartan nearest line point to STF Tjaktja is about 220 m from the hut.
Import should decide whether the endpoint represents the hut POI, the mainline stage boundary, or a hut-spur connector.

end.label: STF Salka Mountain Cabin / Salka section end
caveats: Salka hut coordinate aligns well with OSM section geometry but not exactly with Naturkartan's combined-line endpoint.
Naturkartan appears to use a stage-boundary convention near Salka that may align with the next Salka-Singi section rather than the hut centroid.

sections.name: Salka-Singi

difficulty.label: Easy-to-moderate valley stage; no formal official grade found
difficulty.source: STF and Naturkartan describe easy and mostly flat walking over heath and moorland, with bridges, broad valley views and a more winding/rocky approach to Singi. Field reports agree the tread is generally easy-to-moderate but emphasize exposed wind and weather.

notes: Official STF section direction is Salka to Singi.
This is STF Abisko-Nikkaluokta stage 5 and Naturkartan route BD38.
The section overlaps Kungsleden and Nordkalottleden context.
Singi is a major junction: official Kungsleden continues south toward Kaitumjaure, while the popular Kebnekaise/Nikkaluokta route leaves official Kungsleden at Singi.
No ferry or boat belongs directly to this section. The Laddjujavri boat is an access aid on the distant Nikkaluokta-Kebnekaise approach, not section geometry.

start.label: STF Salka Mountain Cabin / Salka section start
caveats: Naturkartan's Salka start is materially offset from the STF hut and may be an intentional stage-break or junction convention.
OSM relation 17080095 and a secondary GPX align much closer to the hut and to the previous OSM Tjaktja-Salka endpoint.
Later import must decide whether the canonical endpoint is the hut POI, OSM shared section node, or Naturkartan stage-break point.

end.label: STF Singi Mountain Cabin / Singi section end
caveats: Singi is both a hut and a trail junction. OSM uses a shared node for the continuing Singi-Kaitumjaure mainline and Kebnekaise connector.
Naturkartan uses a short Singi spur linking its main end to nearby continuation starts.
Later import should keep Singi junction/connector metadata separate from the hut POI if the geometry requires it.

sections.name: Singi-Kaitumjaure

difficulty.label: Easy mountain stage; no formal grade beyond official descriptive wording
difficulty.source: STF calls this an easy stage and Naturkartan describes easy walking with small elevation changes. Field reports agree that the walking is generally straightforward, but weather, boardwalk condition, mosquitoes and the final birch/boardwalk approach can make it feel harder.
caveats: STF lists 4-5 hours; Naturkartan Swedish/API evidence lists 4-6 hours and English text was reported as 5-6 hours in the geometry lane.
Difficulty can increase with cold wind, rain, early-season snow patches, worn boardwalks and mosquitoes around lower/birch areas.

notes: Official direction is Singi to Kaitumjaure.
This is the candidate mainline continuation after Salka-Singi and STF Nikkaluokta-Saltoluokta stage 3.
Singi is also the junction where the Kebnekaise/Nikkaluokta access route leaves or joins the Kungsleden mainline; keep that as connector/access metadata.
Kaitumjaure is a remote hut endpoint before the next mainline stage toward Teusajaure.

start.label: STF Singi Mountain Cabin / Singi section start
caveats: Singi is both a hut and trail junction. Keep hut POI coordinates separate from route geometry endpoints unless normalization requires snapped hut endpoints.
The eastbound Kebnekaise/Nikkaluokta route is connector/access metadata, not the Kungsleden mainline continuation.

end.label: STF Kaitumjaure Mountain Cabin / Kaitumjaure section end
caveats: No material endpoint gap was found; differences are normal hut POI versus route endpoint conventions.
Kaitumjaure is the shared endpoint for the following Kaitumjaure-Teusajaure section; later normalization should deduplicate the hut POI and route junction.

sourceSummary.classification: planning-grade

caveats: STF lists 4-5 hours; Naturkartan Swedish/API evidence lists 4-6 hours and English text was reported as 5-6 hours.

sections.name: Kaitumjaure-Teusajaure
sections.estimatedTime: 3-5 or 4-5 hours depending on official source

difficulty.label: Mostly easy fell stage with rocky, exposed and steep sections
difficulty.source: STF and Naturkartan describe a short stage that is mostly easy/open fell walking, but both official text and field reports note stone/rock near the start, possible wet sections, limited water on Muorki and a steep rocky final descent to Teusajaure.
caveats: STF route overview lists 4-5 hours while the STF section page/Naturkartan lane reported 3-5 hours.
AllTrails reviewers called the segment easy, but blogs and field reports call the climb/descent rocky, stony, tiring or weather-dependent.
Wind on the plateau and wind/waves at Teusajaure can materially change the practical difficulty even when the footpath is passable.

notes: Official direction is Kaitumjaure to Teusajaure.
This is STF Nikkaluokta-Saltoluokta stage 4 and the candidate Kungsleden mainline continuation after Singi-Kaitumjaure.
Teusajaure lake crossing is not part of this hiking section geometry; model it as access/connector metadata for the next Teusajaure-Vakkotavare section.
The stage passes into Sjaunja/Sjavnja and Laponia context between Gaidumjohka and Teusajaure.

sourceSummary.classification: planning-grade

caveats: STF route overview lists 9 km, 4-5 hours; STF section page and Naturkartan were reported as 3-5 hours.

sections.name: Teusajaure-Vakkotavare
sections.estimatedTime: 4-6 hours by STF; 5-6 or 5-7 hours in other official/secondary evidence

difficulty.label: Moderate mountain stage because of boat logistics and elevation change despite straightforward trail
difficulty.source: STF and Naturkartan describe the route as generally straightforward after a required Teusajaure crossing, with a long climb from birch forest to open fell/heath and a steep switchbacking descent to Vakkotavare. Field reports stress rowing effort, mud/high terrain in places and a steep/slippery final descent.
caveats: The Teusajaure lake crossing can be physically hard when self-rowing and may be unsafe or cancelled in wind or unsuitable water levels.
Time estimates conflict: STF route evidence says 4-6 hours, Naturkartan says 5-6 hours and an STF English snippet/secondary guides may show 5-7 hours.
The section ends at a roadhead, but Vakkotavare has no shop/resupply according to current STF route and shop-list evidence.

notes: Official direction is Teusajaure to Vakkotavare.
The section begins with the Dievssajavri/Teusajaure boat or rowboat crossing from the hut/north shore to the south landing.
The walking portion after the crossing enters Stora Sjofallet/Stuor Muorkke National Park within Laponia World Heritage.
Southbound continuation after Vakkotavare is a road/bus and Kebnats-Saltoluokta boat transfer before the next mapped walking stage at Saltoluokta.

sourceSummary.classification: planning-grade

caveats: STF Swedish route gives 4-6 hours; Naturkartan gives 5-6 hours; rules lane saw STF stage as 5-7 hours and field lane notes secondary guides often say 5-7.

sections.name: Saltoluokta-Sitojaure

difficulty.label: Moderate mountain stage with steep initial climb, exposed plateau and remote roadless endpoint
difficulty.source: STF and Naturkartan describe an easy-going trail surface but a fairly steep climb from Saltoluokta, open mountain/heath terrain, Autsutjvagge shelter about halfway and descent toward STF Sitojaure.

Early route-finding from Saltoluokta has several branching/parallel paths; Naturkartan warns hikers to keep left on Kungsleden after side-trail junctions.

Elevation figures conflict across secondary sources; do not import ascent/descent until the final selected geometry is profiled.
